+# Maximum number of arguments Coraza will parse per request, across the query
+# string, the path and the request body. Arguments beyond the limit are
+# dropped, which is why rules 200004 and 200005 below reject a request that
+# reaches it: silently dropped arguments are invisible to every ARGS rule.
+# Keep this as low as the applications behind Coraza allow.
+# For JSON bodies, this same flag can also trip below the configured count:
+# the flattened form of a JSON body is capped at a multiple of the body's own
+# size, so a body whose fields share a few very long parent keys across many
+# leaves can hit that cap first. That is expected -- it bounds memory that the
+# argument count alone can't see -- but if legitimate JSON traffic denies here
+# without the argument count itself looking high, that byte cap is why.
# Maximum request body size (bytes) Coraza will accept for buffering. When
